members.name: Does cybersecurity adequately address privacy harms caused by digital systems and security interventions?

themes.name: Does HIPAA's institutional and rule-based model adequately protect individuals' health-information privacy?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether HIPAA's Privacy Rule sufficiently governs health-data collection, disclosure, secondary use, and individual control.

members.name: Does HIPAA's institutional and rule-based model adequately protect individuals' health-information privacy?

themes.name: Do stronger privacy protections increase trust and willingness to share sensitive personal or health information?
themes.definition: This question investigates the relationship between privacy safeguards, perceived vulnerability, institutional trust, and individuals' decisions to disclose valuable information.

members.name: Do stronger privacy protections increase trust and willingness to share sensitive personal or health information?

themes.name: Do privacy rules create incentives that unintentionally increase collection, disclosure, or surveillance?
themes.definition: This question analyzes whether legal requirements, market structures, and organizational practices designed to protect privacy can instead encourage additional data accumulation or monitoring.

members.name: Do privacy rules create incentives that unintentionally increase collection, disclosure, or surveillance?

themes.name: Do privacy protections for personally identifying information adequately address online identity theft and financial harm?
themes.definition: This question examines whether legal rules prevent unauthorized acquisition, disclosure, aggregation, and reuse of identifying data in ways that enable fraud or other concrete harms.

members.name: Do privacy protections for personally identifying information adequately address online identity theft and financial harm?

themes.name: Do organizations entrusted with sensitive personal information or biological materials owe heightened privacy duties?
themes.definition: This question examines whether vulnerability, sensitivity, or the entrusted nature of information justifies stronger safeguards and remedies than ordinary data handling.

members.name: Do organizations entrusted with sensitive personal information or biological materials owe heightened privacy duties?

themes.name: Do online intermediaries' adhesion contracts fairly allocate rights over users' personal data?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether standardized platform terms meaningfully protect users or instead entrench unequal bargaining power between individuals and data-collecting organizations.

members.name: Do online intermediaries' adhesion contracts fairly allocate rights over users' personal data?

themes.name: Do notice, consent, and privacy-oriented interface design produce meaningful understanding and trust in online data-dependent services?
themes.definition: This question tests whether formal disclosures and user-facing choices actually influence behavior, perceived risk, fairness judgments, and confidence in digital systems.

members.name: Do notice, consent, and privacy-oriented interface design produce meaningful understanding and trust in online data-dependent services?

themes.name: Do health and genetic data require special privacy protections because their disclosure can produce discrimination or group stigmatization?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether sensitive biomedical information presents distinctive risks that ordinary informational-privacy rules cannot adequately address.

members.name: Do health and genetic data require special privacy protections because their disclosure can produce discrimination or group stigmatization?

themes.name: Do existing remedies adequately address inaccurate, improperly handled, or unauthorizedly disclosed consumer data?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether affected individuals can obtain effective correction, dispute resolution, compensation, or other relief for data-related harms.

members.name: Do existing remedies adequately address inaccurate, improperly handled, or unauthorizedly disclosed consumer data?

themes.name: Do existing legal regimes adequately protect highly intimate, sexual, child-related, and student information from unauthorized disclosure or misuse?
themes.definition: This question focuses on whether specialized protections and remedies address especially vulnerable individuals and sensitive forms of personal information.

members.name: Do existing legal regimes adequately protect highly intimate, sexual, child-related, and student information from unauthorized disclosure or misuse?

themes.name: Do existing cybersecurity and breach-notification rules adequately protect against nonfinancial and nonphysical privacy harms?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether law sufficiently addresses reputational, dignitary, emotional, autonomy-related, and other consequences of unauthorized access or disclosure.

members.name: Do existing cybersecurity and breach-notification rules adequately protect against nonfinancial and nonphysical privacy harms?

themes.name: Do cross-border data flows allow powerful technology firms and jurisdictions to impose privacy standards beyond their borders?
themes.definition: This question concerns the extraterritorial effects of transnational platforms, conflicting national regimes, and international movement of personal information.

members.name: Do cross-border data flows allow powerful technology firms and jurisdictions to impose privacy standards beyond their borders?

themes.name: Do consumer-facing procedures and increased enforcement measurably reduce privacy harms online?
themes.definition: This question calls for empirical evaluation of whether notices, consent interfaces, complaint systems, enforcement actions, and other interventions change behavior or reduce actual privacy-related harm.

members.name: Do consumer-facing procedures and increased enforcement measurably reduce privacy harms online?

themes.name: Do concentrated corporate control over identity and behavioral data create risks of inequality, manipulation, or democratic distortion?
themes.definition: This question examines whether powerful digital intermediaries and data-intensive firms use classification, personalization, or influence in ways that undermine equal treatment, consumer autonomy, or public discourse.

members.name: Do concentrated corporate control over identity and behavioral data create risks of inequality, manipulation, or democratic distortion?

themes.name: Do computerized data-processing systems produce erroneous or unjust government judgments despite their appearance of objectivity?
themes.definition: This question examines whether aggregation, profiling, and automated analysis can distort institutional decisions and whether privacy or data-governance rules should address those errors.

members.name: Do computerized data-processing systems produce erroneous or unjust government judgments despite their appearance of objectivity?

themes.name: Do First Amendment doctrines unduly restrict remedies for technology-enabled privacy harms?
themes.definition: This question focuses on whether constitutional protections for speech and information dissemination prevent effective regulation of harmful disclosures and data practices.

members.name: Do First Amendment doctrines unduly restrict remedies for technology-enabled privacy harms?

themes.name: Can transparency, system design, and technical safeguards compensate for individuals' limited ability to understand data practices?
themes.definition: This question examines whether privacy-enhancing technologies, access controls, clearer communication, and accountable institutional design can supplement or replace ineffective consent.

members.name: Can transparency, system design, and technical safeguards compensate for individuals' limited ability to understand data practices?

themes.name: Can state-level or coordinated privacy legislation effectively fill gaps created by fragmented federal and cross-border information-governance regimes?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether uniform legislation, state regulation, or institutional coordination can improve coherence without sacrificing context-sensitive protection.

members.name: Can state-level or coordinated privacy legislation effectively fill gaps created by fragmented federal and cross-border information-governance regimes?

themes.name: Can regulatory enforcement, including FTC orders and consent decrees, effectively change organizations' data practices?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether administrative enforcement creates substantive and practically enforceable privacy and data-security obligations beyond formal statutory rules.

members.name: Can regulatory enforcement, including FTC orders and consent decrees, effectively change organizations' data practices?

themes.name: Can public disclosure and publicity effectively remedy organizational wrongdoing without creating disproportionate privacy harms?
themes.definition: This question evaluates disclosure as an accountability mechanism while considering retaliation, humiliation, exposure, and the privacy interests of affected individuals.

members.name: Can public disclosure and publicity effectively remedy organizational wrongdoing without creating disproportionate privacy harms?

themes.name: Can property or contract law provide an adequate foundation for rights in personal information?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether personal data should be treated as alienable property or governed through ordinary agreements, rather than through specialized privacy and data-protection duties.

members.name: Can property or contract law provide an adequate foundation for rights in personal information?

themes.name: Can private-law institutions and distributed governance complement public regulation of personal data?
themes.definition: This question examines the respective roles of contracts, torts, fiduciary duties, companies, civil-society organizations, local networks, and regulators in allocating privacy responsibilities.

members.name: Can private-law institutions and distributed governance complement public regulation of personal data?

themes.name: Can privacy torts provide better remedies for dignitary and psychological harms than defamation law?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether civil privacy claims should recognize non-economic injuries arising from truthful publication, unwanted identification, exposure, or misuse of personal information.

members.name: Can privacy torts provide better remedies for dignitary and psychological harms than defamation law?

themes.name: Can privacy and security objectives conflict in the design of data systems?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether privacy restrictions can impede safety, investigation, or cybersecurity, and whether extensive collection creates new security, physical-safety, or misuse risks.

members.name: Can privacy and security objectives conflict in the design of data systems?

themes.name: Can government-controlled records and digital credentials improperly determine people's ability to exercise rights and participate in society?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether identification, authentication, and official record systems create privacy and autonomy risks by conditioning access to legal or social benefits.

members.name: Can government-controlled records and digital credentials improperly determine people's ability to exercise rights and participate in society?

themes.name: Can cooperative, adaptive governance outperform adversarial and politically dominated approaches to privacy regulation?
themes.definition: This question compares process-oriented compliance, specialized expertise, industry participation, and public-private cooperation with conventional command-and-control regulation.

members.name: Can cooperative, adaptive governance outperform adversarial and politically dominated approaches to privacy regulation?

themes.name: Can connected devices and pervasive sensors improve public safety without making privacy an unavoidable sacrifice?
themes.definition: This question investigates how networked technologies that interact with the physical world should be designed and regulated to reconcile security benefits with privacy risks.

members.name: Can connected devices and pervasive sensors improve public safety without making privacy an unavoidable sacrifice?

themes.name: Are sector-specific privacy laws adequate for data practices that cross institutional and technological boundaries?
themes.definition: This question tests whether protections organized around particular industries or information categories can govern data flows involving multiple sectors and private technology companies.

members.name: Are sector-specific privacy laws adequate for data practices that cross institutional and technological boundaries?

themes.name: Are existing cybersecurity and privacy rules sufficiently preventive and effective against emerging data-driven harms?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether current safeguards, institutional enforcement, and remedies address risks before and after unauthorized access, disclosure, or misuse.

members.name: Are existing cybersecurity and privacy rules sufficiently preventive and effective against emerging data-driven harms?

themes.name: Are current cybersecurity and data-security rules sufficient to prevent privacy harms caused by organizational failures?
themes.definition: This question distinguishes security breaches and negligent data protection from privacy regulation and evaluates whether existing law deters firms and governments from mishandling stored personal information.

members.name: Are current cybersecurity and data-security rules sufficient to prevent privacy harms caused by organizational failures?

themes.name: Are confidentiality policies and access controls sufficient to prevent privacy harms in large data systems?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether security and risk-reduction measures can reliably protect data or merely limit some forms of unauthorized access and disclosure.

members.name: Are confidentiality policies and access controls sufficient to prevent privacy harms in large data systems?

themes.name: Are biometric and identification technologies more effective as privacy safeguards or as tools of surveillance?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the circumstances in which identification systems can protect anonymity or security versus enabling persistent tracking and loss of privacy.

members.name: Are biometric and identification technologies more effective as privacy safeguards or as tools of surveillance?
